**This chapter closes [Studio 2: Govern the work and declare your question](studio02-govern-the-work.qmd).** Its lessons each ended at **It is your turn**; what you wrote there arrives here as working material, and this is where the pieces become one artifact you can defend.

**What this milestone produces.** Your working agreement (a responsibility statement, your working rules, your opened AI Research Ledger, your delegation map, and the red-flag screen of your chosen problem) and your question, formally declared: objective, units, outcomes and conditions, kind and reach, and a provisional claim boundary.

## What you bring

Check you are carrying each of these before you start. If one is missing, go back and work that lesson's **It is your turn** first; the practice below assumes it.

- [Lesson 2 — AI Is Your Arm, Not Your Brain](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/01-ai-is-your-arm-not-your-brain.html): your opened AI Research Ledger with its first verified exchange, run on your own problem's key fact.
- [Lesson 3 — The Student as Research Director](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/02-the-student-as-research-director.html): your delegation map: the road's tasks sorted into safe to delegate, delegate then verify, and never delegate.
- [Lesson 4 — Specify, Delegate, Interrogate, Inspect, Verify, Document, Defend](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/03-specify-delegate-interrogate-inspect-verify-document-defend.html): one complete SDIIVDD run on a checkable claim, with the verification you ran and what it caught.
- [Lesson 5 — Research Responsibility and Intellectual Ownership](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/04-research-responsibility-and-intellectual-ownership.html): your ownership statement, your never-delegate list, and a first draft of your AI-use disclosure.
- [Lesson 6 — Descriptive, Predictive, and Causal Questions](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part2-curiosity-to-design/06-descriptive-predictive-and-causal-questions.html): your lead question placed by kind and reach, double-barrels split, with its comparison world written out if the question is causal: the arc's fourth beat, closed.

## The practice {#milestone}

1. Write your responsibility statement: the decisions that stay yours no matter how good the tool gets.
2. Write your working rules: what you will delegate, what you will always verify, and how you will record both.
3. Open your AI Research Ledger and give its first rows to the exchanges you have already run, the Studio 1 brainstorm included.
4. Run the red-flag screen on your chosen problem: is it answerable, is it yours to ask, and could you defend attempting it.
5. Declare your objective, your units, your outcome, and the conditions you are comparing or describing.
6. Declare kind and reach, and write the words in your question that fix each one.
7. Write your provisional claim boundary: the sentence you hope to defend, and the sentence you will not be able to.

## A version, not a pass

Your milestone artifact is a dated, numbered **version** with the reason for the version attached. When later evidence changes it, you write the next version rather than editing the last one, because the sequence of changes is itself part of your research record.

## The four rails, here

Four concerns cross every studio in this book. At this milestone they take these specific forms.

- **Ethics, permissions, and data exposure.** The red-flag screen runs here, and a problem that studies people leaves this studio with that fact attached.
- **Evidence, provenance, and reproducibility.** Nothing here is settled until Studio 3 checks it against what is already known.
- **AI activity, verification, and human decisions.** The ledger opens here and every earlier exchange gets its row; from now on, no delegation goes unrecorded.
- **Uncertainty, claim boundary, and revision history.** A question with no recognizable answer cannot carry uncertainty; fix the question before you leave.

## Where this milestone sits

You arrived carrying [Milestone 1: Your curiosity, committed](milestone01-frame-the-inquiry.qmd). Milestone 3 holds the declared question up against what is already known, and it will usually send back a sharper version. The chain ends at [Milestone 12: Your release and next cycle](milestone12-release-next-cycle.qmd), where you decide whether your finished research artifact leaves your hands.

## What sends you back

Studio 3 almost always sends the question back here for a sharper version, and any change in your tools, your data source, or your collaborators reopens the agreement.

## How this milestone is assessed

Each row scores **0**, **1**, or **2**. **12 points total.**

| # | Criterion | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The milestone artifact exists in full, specific to your own project | absent, or generic text that would fit any project | present but incomplete, or specific in some parts and generic in others | complete and unmistakably about your project |
| 2 | The milestone is written as a dated, numbered version with its reason | no version, or a version with no reason given | versioned, but the reason is decorative rather than an account of what changed | versioned with a reason a reader could use to reconstruct your thinking |
| 3 | Every judgment in the artifact is defended by you, not asserted by a tool | conclusions appear with no reasoning, or reproduce a tool's wording | reasoning present but thin where the decision was hardest | each judgment carries a reason you could defend under questioning |
| 4 | The four rails are carried in the form this studio requires | one or more rails absent where this studio required them | all rails present but one is nominal | every rail addressed in the form this studio requires |
| 5 | The milestone's own product is present and defensible: Your working agreement (responsibility statement, working rules, opened AI Research Ledger, delegation map, and the red-flag screen of your chosen problem) and your question, formally declared: objective, units, outcomes and conditions, kind and reach, and a provisional claim boundary | the milestone's own product is missing | present but would not survive a careful question | present and defensible as stated |
| 6 | The declared question is fixed by its own words: kind and reach match the sentence, double-barrels are split, and the claim boundary states both the defensible and the forbidden sentence | no declaration, or a kind or reach the question's words do not fix | declared, but one term is loose enough that a stranger could not say what gets recorded or who the answer is about | declared so a stranger could restate unit, record, and audience, with both boundary sentences present |
